narrative.overview:
The site is the club after last call: the room has gone dark, but the signs are still lit. Every page starts from near-black (`void`) with two faint washes of light in the background, violet from above and blue from the lower right, like a sign glowing off-screen. Against that dark, color is light, not paint. Magenta, violet and blue appear as glows, hairlines, underlines and the one button you are meant to press, never as flat fills behind text.

Density is low and the mood is nocturnal. Content sits in a single 1200px column with generous vertical gaps. Type does the scene-setting: a wide, rounded display face for titles, a narrow technical sans for everything else, and one handwritten flourish in the footer. Album covers are the only imagery and carry most of the color.

The system is allowed to get brighter. Future work may push more neon (gradient rules, glowing panels, tinted washes) where it serves a release, as long as text stays legible and the room stays dark. It must never tip into 80s-parody synthwave, gaming HUD chrome, or a flat streaming-app clone.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black, violet-tinted base with fixed radial light washes.
Neon used as emitted light: glows, 1–2px lines, text-shadow, and one primary action.
Audiowide titles, Rajdhani body and labels, Dancing Script as a single signature.
Pill-shaped controls, softly rounded panels, square-ish fields.
Album cover art as the only imagery.

rules.name: The Light, Not Paint Rule
rules.body: Neon is emitted light: glows, hairlines, outlines, text-shadow and the primary button. Large flat neon fills behind running text are not part of the system. When adding more neon, add it as light around things, not as the background of reading surfaces.

rules.name: The One Magenta Action Rule
rules.body: Each view has at most one magenta-filled control in a group. Everything beside it is a blue-outlined secondary or a ghost button.

rules.name: The Measured Contrast Rule
rules.body: Text stays in `ink-1`, `ink-2` or `ink-3`, or in `magenta` / `cyan`, which pass 4.5:1 on `void`. Blue and violet never carry text below large-text size. Check any new color with the WCAG luminance formula against its real background.

rules.name: The Sign and Readout Rule
rules.body: Audiowide is for names and titles (artist, albums, page headings) at 22px and up. Everything you read in sequence (copy, labels, buttons, data) is Rajdhani. Never set paragraphs in the display face.

rules.name: The Single Signature Rule
rules.body: The script face marks the artist's name once per page, in the footer. It is never a heading, label or button.

rules.name: The Glow Means Live Rule
rules.body: A glow says "this is lit and you can touch it", or it marks the hero title. Static containers don't glow at rest (the contact panel's 9% ambient is the ceiling). Hover and focus may add glow; nothing else should.

dos: **Do** start every surface from `void` with the violet and blue radial washes, and let neon arrive as light: glows, 1–2px lines, text-shadow.
**Do** keep one magenta-filled action per group; use blue-outlined secondary pills for everything else.
**Do** use cyan for information (eyebrows, links, dates) and magenta for action and status.
**Do** set names and titles in the display face at 22px and up, and everything read in sequence in the body face.
**Do** push more neon when a release calls for it (gradient rules, glowing edges, tinted washes), as long as text keeps 4.5:1 against its actual background.
**Do** keep album covers as the dominant imagery, with deep black shadows and colored halos rather than frames.
**Do** respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; motion stays short (120–420ms) on the `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` ease-out.
donts: **Don't** set body copy, labels or small text in Midnight Blue Neon or Afterglow Violet; they fail 4.5:1 on `void`.
**Don't** fill reading surfaces with flat neon or put running text on a neon background.
**Don't** drift into retro synthwave kitsch: no outrun grids, chrome sunsets, palm trees, VHS scanlines or 80s-parody chrome type.
**Don't** borrow gaming or esports UI: no angular HUD frames, notched corners, scan-line overlays or RGB-keyboard rainbow effects.
**Don't** flatten into a generic streaming-app layout: no light theme, no grey card grids, no stock player chrome without the night around it.
**Don't** use the script face anywhere except the artist's name in the footer, and don't add a fourth font family.
**Don't** glow static containers at rest beyond the contact panel's faint ambient; glow is for the lit, the pressable, and the hero title.
